summary: I'm an AI/ML engineer with 2+ years of experience building GCP-native agentic AI systems, LLM-powered applications, RAG workflows and automated ML pipelines. I work across the whole stack that makes AI trustworthy in production: Vertex AI, LangChain, Google ADK, BigQuery, Dataflow, Pub/Sub, GKE and CI/CD.

At Johnson & Johnson (through Pozent) I architected an agentic system that took medical report generation from 2–3 weeks to under a minute, with human reviewers in the loop and their edits feeding back into the system. That mix of hard engineering and close work with the people who use it is exactly what I want to do full time as a Forward Deployed Engineer.

experience.summary: Enterprise AI for a regulated healthcare client: turning slow, manual medical reporting into an automated, reviewable agentic workflow.
bullets: Architected a GCP-native agentic AI system for Medical Impact Assessment reporting, automating PDF and Word generation across structured, semi-structured and unstructured data sources inside secure cloud workflows.
Built AI workflows on Vertex AI, LangChain and Google ADK, orchestrating 5+ agentic steps for retrieval, reasoning, content generation, validation and report assembly at scale.

Built automated ML/AI pipelines with Vertex AI Pipelines and Cloud Composer (Airflow): ingestion (Pub/Sub, Dataflow), transformation (Dataproc, BigQuery) and model evaluation across 2 environments, processing 100,000+ records and 2 Quickbase integrations.

Implemented GCP MLOps: containerized FastAPI/Flask inference services on GKE via CI/CD (Cloud Build / GitHub Actions), with model, prompt and config versioning for reproducible releases and rollbacks.
Set up production model monitoring with Cloud Logging/Monitoring and BigQuery dashboards tracking latency, errors and output quality, with alerts for drift and degradation.

Integrated human-in-the-loop review and RLHF-inspired feedback loops, using reviewer edits and approvals as labeled feedback to refine prompts and retrieval and drive periodic re-evaluation, cutting report generation from 2–3 weeks to under 1 minute.

experience.summary: Led a student engineering team turning legacy scientific tools into a modern analytics platform.
bullets: Led development of MeltShiny, transforming 2 legacy research tools into a cross-platform analytics platform for automated DNA/RNA thermodynamic modeling and reproducible scientific analysis at scale.
Engineered reactive R pipelines with MeltR to process melt-curve datasets, apply nonlinear curve fitting, detect outliers and extract 4 ML-ready thermodynamic features for downstream analytics.
Implemented Dockerized deployment and GitHub Actions CI/CD, improving reproducibility across contributors; guided 4 undergraduates through 10+ sprints and reviewed 30+ pull requests.

experience.summary: First production ML: forecasting late payments for collections teams.
bullets: Trained and compared supervised ML models (Linear/Ridge Regression, Random Forest, Gradient Boosting) on 50,000+ historical invoices to forecast payment delays and DSO trends for collections.
Engineered 15+ features and tuned scikit-learn models via GridSearchCV and cross-validation, tracking MAE/RMSE against baselines.

Deployed the model as a Python/Flask prediction service for the Spring Boot backend, with periodic retraining on new data; containerized with Docker (98% CI/CD success) and tested with PyTest (80%+ coverage).

caseStudy.title: Agentic Medical Impact Assessment, in under a minute
caseStudy.problem: Medical Impact Assessment reports took 2–3 weeks to produce. Evidence lived in structured tables, semi-structured documents and unstructured PDFs, and everything had to be reviewable and auditable.
caseStudy.approach: A GCP-native agentic system: ingestion pipelines make the data model-ready, a multi-step agent graph retrieves, reasons and drafts, validators check the output, and a human reviewer approves. Their edits become labeled feedback that improves the next draft.
caseStudy.result: Report generation dropped from 2–3 weeks to under a minute, with reviewers still in control.
caseStudy.confidentialityNote: Client-confidential details are intentionally omitted. This is a faithful, generalized view of the architecture.

pipeline.label: Ingest
pipeline.detail: Event-driven ingestion from source systems into the platform. Streaming and batch paths feed the same downstream tables.

pipeline.label: Transform
pipeline.detail: Structured, semi-structured and unstructured inputs are normalized and made model-ready. Orchestrated by Cloud Composer (Airflow) across 2 environments, 100,000+ records.

pipeline.label: Retrieve
pipeline.detail: An agent step pulls the right evidence for each report section instead of stuffing everything into one prompt.

pipeline.label: Reason & draft
pipeline.detail: 5+ agentic steps handle reasoning, content generation and section assembly, each with a narrow, testable job.

pipeline.label: Validate
pipeline.detail: Automated validation catches structural and content problems before a human ever sees the draft.

pipeline.label: Human review
pipeline.detail: Reviewers edit and approve. Their changes are stored as labeled feedback used to refine prompts and retrieval and to trigger periodic re-evaluation.

pipeline.label: Deliver
pipeline.detail: Final reports are generated as PDF and Word documents, and integrated with Quickbase (2 integrations).

pipeline.label: Operate
pipeline.detail: FastAPI/Flask services run on GKE via Cloud Build / GitHub Actions with versioned models, prompts and config. Cloud Logging/Monitoring and BigQuery dashboards track latency, errors and output quality.

projects.name: Agentic Market Researcher
projects.tagline: Multi-agent research platform: 3+ hours of analyst work in one click.
projects.problem: Market research means reading dozens of news items, SEC/EDGAR filings and social threads, then reconciling them. It's slow, and easy to do inconsistently.
how: Asynchronous Python ETL pulls 20+ sources (news, SEC/EDGAR, Reddit) in parallel.
Claude Haiku agents do the cheap, wide work (triage, extraction); Claude Sonnet agents do the synthesis.
Prompt caching keeps repeated context cheap; weighted ranking puts the most credible signals first.
Structured outputs and one-click insights replace manual note-taking.
projects.impact: Replaces 3+ hours of manual research with a single click.

projects.name: Insurance RAG Assistant
projects.tagline: Upload insurance PDFs, ask in plain English, get answers grounded in the documents.
projects.problem: Policy documents are long, dense and full of exceptions. People need the deductible or exclusion for their situation, quickly, with proof.
how: PyMuPDF extracts text; sentence-aware chunking (800 chars, 150 overlap) preserves context.
Chunks are embedded locally with all-MiniLM-L6-v2 and stored in a persistent ChromaDB with filename metadata.
Questions are embedded, matched by cosine similarity (top-6), and passed to an LLM that answers with source citations.
FastAPI backend with upload / list / delete / chat / debug-search endpoints; React + Vite + Tailwind frontend; Docker Compose for one-command deploys.
projects.impact: A complete, deployable full-stack RAG app: ingestion, retrieval, grounded answers and a document manager.

projects.name: End-to-End ML Pipeline on GCP
projects.tagline: Ingest → features → train → evaluate → register → deploy, with drift-triggered retraining.
projects.problem: Models rot. Without automation and monitoring, nobody notices until the output is wrong.
how: A Vertex AI Pipelines workflow ingests data from BigQuery, engineers features, trains and evaluates candidates, then registers and deploys the best one.
Compares Logistic Regression, Random Forest and XGBoost.
The winner is served through FastAPI on a Vertex endpoint / GKE.
Drift monitoring triggers the pipeline to re-run when metrics or drift cross a threshold.
projects.impact: A hands-off train → deploy → monitor → retrain loop.

projects.name: AI SQL Data Retrieval Agent
projects.tagline: Ask your database questions in English.
projects.problem: Business users have questions; the answers sit in SQL tables they can't query.
how: A 3-stage LangChain workflow: generate the SQL, execute it, then format the result for humans.
Handles 5+ query types across 10+ PostgreSQL tables.
FastAPI backend with a React visualization interface.
projects.impact: Natural-language access to 10+ tables without writing SQL.

projects.name: “Ask my AI” on my GitHub profile
projects.tagline: A recruiter-facing agent that runs entirely on GitHub Issues and Actions.
how: A visitor opens a pre-filled issue; a GitHub Action calls a free LLM grounded in a curated knowledge base and replies on the issue.
Strict grounding rules, skill-level honesty (core / working / familiar), per-user and global daily caps, and sanitized output.
A 'job-fit check' compares a pasted job description against the knowledge base and reports evidence and gaps, honestly.
projects.impact: The same idea powers the AI on this site, with a richer UI.

projects.name: MeltShiny
projects.tagline: Cross-platform DNA/RNA thermodynamic analytics for researchers.
projects.status: Open Source with SLU · tech lead
projects.problem: Two legacy research tools made reproducible thermodynamic analysis hard.
how: Reactive R pipelines (MeltR) process melt curves, fit nonlinear models and flag outliers.
Extracts 4 ML-ready thermodynamic features.
Dockerized, with GitHub Actions CI/CD; led a team of 4 undergraduates through 10+ sprints and reviewed 30+ pull requests.
projects.impact: Two tools merged into one reproducible platform.

projects.name: NVIDIA NIM Multi-document RAG
projects.tagline: Multi-document retrieval and answers on NVIDIA NIM models.
projects.problem: Answering across several documents needs retrieval that scales beyond one PDF.
how: Multi-document RAG pipeline built on NVIDIA NIM (NeMo Inference Microservices).
Streamlit front end, deployed publicly.

projects.name: LLM Systems Field Manuals
projects.tagline: Open guides: six production LLM patterns on Google Cloud, RAG field notes, retrieval trade-offs.
projects.problem: Teams adopt LLMs faster than they learn the trade-offs.
how: LLMOps-Guide: 'Six LLM patterns' with runnable starters on Google Cloud.
RAG_QnA: chunking, embeddings, vector databases, retrieval techniques, multi-tenancy and evaluation.
LLM_tradeoffs: how vector retrieval finds things (HNSW / IVF), speed-accuracy-memory trade-offs, agentic frameworks, which LLM for which job.
projects.impact: Teaching what I build, which is also how I explain AI to clients.

projects.name: Murmur: PDF to audiobook
projects.tagline: Drop in a book, get back an audiobook with chapters. Free, private, fully local.
projects.problem: Turning a long PDF into good audio means more than text-to-speech: front matter, running headers, captions and technical content all ruin the listening experience.
how: Validates the file by content, then samples pages to judge whether the book works as audio (prose vs figures).
A narration 'director' strips front/back matter, headers, footers and captions, rejoins hyphenation, finds chapters from the outline or headings, and starts at the story.
Rules run offline; an optional AI layer refines judgment calls. Narrates sentence by sentence with deliberate pauses using local TTS (Kokoro, Piper or eSpeak), or a cloned voice.
Packages an .m4b with chapter markers and cover art (or MP3 / zipped chapters). FastAPI service and CLI, Docker, CI.
projects.impact: End-to-end local pipeline: $0 per book, no accounts or API keys.

projects.name: ChatABT: agentic chat platform
projects.tagline: A ChatGPT-style app on open-weight models, with project-aware agent tools.
projects.problem: Most chat UIs are demos. I wanted a production-shaped platform: streaming, branching, code-aware agents, auth, jobs and persistence.
how: React + TypeScript + Tailwind front end: streaming with stop, reasoning panel, message branching (edit, regenerate), markdown, code, math and citations.
FastAPI back end on open-weight models via OpenRouter, with a live model catalogue, tool calling and automatic titles.
Project folders: upload a folder, zip or GitHub repo; the server chunks and embeds code (hybrid vector + keyword search) and gives the model agent tools (list_files, read_file, grep, search_code).

Postgres + pgvector, Redis, MinIO, ARQ workers, JWT with rotating refresh tokens, OAuth SSO (Google, Microsoft, GitHub), SearXNG web search, memory, image generation. Runs offline on a mock backend too.
projects.impact: A complete agent platform: UI, API, retrieval, jobs and auth, all containerized.

projects.name: AI Full-Stack Chat App
projects.tagline: A compact, production-shaped chat app with a pluggable LLM layer.
projects.problem: Prototypes hard-wire one model provider and skip tests, history and deployment.
how: FastAPI backend, dependency-free web UI and SQLite-backed multi-conversation history.
Provider-agnostic LLM client: OpenAI, Groq, OpenRouter or a local Ollama server, plus an offline echo provider so it runs with no key.
Typed REST API with validation and clean error handling, XSS-safe rendering, a bounded history window, pytest suite, Dockerfile and CI.
projects.impact: Runs end to end with no API key; swaps providers by configuration.

projects.name: Conversational RAG over PDFs
projects.tagline: Upload PDFs and hold a follow-up conversation grounded in them.
projects.problem: Follow-up questions ('what about the second one?') break naive RAG because they lose context.
how: PDFs are chunked, embedded (all-MiniLM-L6-v2) and indexed in Chroma, re-indexing only when files change.
A history-aware retriever rewrites each follow-up into a standalone query before retrieval.
Groq-hosted models answer with sources shown under each answer; history is kept per session.
projects.impact: Multi-turn grounded Q&A with visible sources.

projects.name: Quickbase → GCS → BigQuery tool
projects.tagline: A reliable data-migration tool: extract, stage, load.
projects.problem: Getting application data into the warehouse needs complete, restartable extraction, not a one-off script.
how: Paginated, retrying extraction from the Quickbase REST API, streamed to GCS as gzip NDJSON (memory-safe).
Optional BigQuery load with an autodetected schema; service-account or ADC auth.
Typed config, unit-tested extraction logic, CI.

projects.name: CrewAI researcher + writer
projects.tagline: Two collaborating agents turn a YouTube channel into a blog post.
projects.problem: Single-prompt content generation is shallow; research and writing are separate jobs.
how: A researcher agent mines a YouTube channel for a topic using a RAG search tool.
A writer agent turns the findings into a Markdown blog post.

fde.title: How I work with customers
fde.intro: A Forward Deployed Engineer is an engineer who goes to where the problem is. These are the habits I bring to that job. Try them live below.

steps.title: Discover
steps.summary: Listen first. Get the real problem, not the requested solution.
steps.detail: I run short, structured conversations with the people who do the work: what takes the time, where it goes wrong, who signs off, what happens when it's late. I ask for a real example and walk through it step by step.
steps.output: A one-page problem statement everyone agrees with.

steps.title: Diagnose
steps.summary: Find the pain points and where AI actually helps.
steps.detail: I map the workflow end to end and mark each step: repetitive and rule-like (automate), language-heavy (LLM), judgment-heavy (keep a human, support them), risky (add a gate). Not everything should be AI, and saying that early builds trust.
steps.output: A workflow map with candidate AI insertion points ranked by value and risk.

steps.title: Design
steps.summary: Pick the thinnest slice that proves value and keeps people in control.
steps.detail: Data access, evaluation criteria, human-in-the-loop review, failure behaviour, cost and latency. I explain the trade-offs in plain language so decisions get made quickly.
steps.output: A scoped plan with success metrics and a review process.

steps.title: Deploy
steps.summary: Ship into the real environment, with CI/CD and monitoring from day one.
steps.detail: Containerized services, versioned prompts and models, rollbacks, dashboards for latency, errors and output quality. The same practices I used on GKE and Vertex AI at J&J.
steps.output: A working system in the customer's environment.

steps.title: Embed & iterate
steps.summary: Stay close. Turn user feedback into the next release.
steps.detail: Reviewer edits and approvals become labeled feedback that improves prompts and retrieval. I keep checking what users actually do, then widen the scope once trust is earned.
steps.output: Adoption, a feedback loop, and the next workflow to tackle.

strengths.title: Clear communicator
strengths.text: I explain models, trade-offs and limitations in plain language, to engineers, domain experts and executives alike.

strengths.title: Pain-point detective
strengths.text: I ask about the last time it went wrong, not about features. The cost is usually hiding in handoffs and rework.

strengths.title: Honest about limits
strengths.text: I'd rather tell you AI is the wrong tool for a step than ship something nobody trusts.

strengths.title: Team leader
strengths.text: I led a student team through 10+ sprints and reviewed 30+ pull requests, which means giving direction and feedback clearly.

painSigns: People ask the same questions repeatedly
Answers are buried in long PDFs
aiFit: Answers with citations to the source passage
Say 'I don't know' when the documents don't cover it
patterns.humanGate: Citations let users verify; low-confidence answers route to a person.

patterns.name: Research & signal synthesis
painSigns: Analysts spend hours reading before they can think
aiFit: Cheap models triage, strong models synthesize
patterns.humanGate: Analyst reviews the synthesis and the cited sources before acting.

patterns.name: Ask-your-data (natural-language analytics)
painSigns: Business users wait on analysts for simple questions
A backlog of ad-hoc data requests
patterns.humanGate: Show the generated query; read-only credentials; analysts review new query patterns.

proof.claim: 5+ query types across 10+ PostgreSQL tables in plain English

patterns.name: Forecasting & predictive operations
painSigns: Decisions made on gut feel or stale spreadsheets
A model exists but nobody monitors it
aiFit: Compare simple baselines to boosted models
patterns.humanGate: Thresholds and alerts route anomalies to an owner; models are versioned for rollback.

proof.claim: Vertex AI Pipelines with drift-triggered retraining; earlier, forecasting payment delays on 50,000+ invoices at HighRadius

patterns.name: Intake, triage & routing
painSigns: Humans read and sort every incoming item
patterns.humanGate: Low-confidence items go to people; corrections feed an evaluation set.

proof.claim: Same agentic building blocks: structured extraction, validation and human review at scale

discoveryQuestions: Walk me through the last time this went wrong, step by step.
Who touches this work, and who signs off on it?
How long does it take today, and how long should it take?
What data is involved, and where does it live?
What would make you not trust an AI's answer?
What does 'done well' look like in numbers you already track?
